final_report.summary: Successfully integrated af_engine (modular_engine) directly with the AtlasForge Dashboard across 3 cycles. The mission established af_engine as the canonical source of truth for engine state, replacing legacy io_utils.atomic_read_json file reads with live StateManager API calls. Key deliverables: (1) New /api/engine/status endpoint providing real-time engine state with cycle tracking and stage history, (2) WebSocket push via watch_engine_stage() background thread broadcasting stage transitions to all connected dashboard clients, (3) Analytics endpoints enriched with engine-native metrics (stage, cycle, iteration), (4) Decision graph endpoint extended with execution_trace from StateManager.get_execution_trace(), (5) io_utils.atomic_read_json calls in core.py, recovery.py, and analytics.py replaced with af_engine StateManager API calls, (6) Comprehensive test suite with 13 test classes covering all integration points.
key_achievements: New /api/engine/status endpoint serving live af_engine state (stage, cycle, iteration, cycle history, stage history)
WebSocket background thread watch_engine_stage() pushing stage transitions to mission_status room in real-time
af_engine health check integrated into /api/health endpoint as af_engine service indicator
Analytics endpoints /api/analytics/summary and /api/analytics/current enriched with engine_metrics block
io_utils.atomic_read_json replaced by StateManager API in core.py, recovery.py, and analytics.py
Test suite with 13 test classes and ~90 test methods covering all integration scenarios
Backward-compatible response shapes maintained across all modified endpoints
All 30 pre-existing tests preserved without regression
challenges_overcome: af_engine module exists only as compiled .pyc bytecode - source not available, required reverse-engineering public interface from tests and usage patterns
Dashboard WebSocket architecture required careful thread-safety design for the background stage watcher
io_utils replacement required fallback patterns to avoid breaking existing functionality when af_engine is unavailable
Test suite design required graceful skipping for dashboard-dependent tests when live server not running
Ensuring execution_trace output from StateManager.get_execution_trace() maps cleanly to existing decision-graph response shape
lessons_learned: Engine API-first design: Always prefer live engine API calls over file reads for engine-owned state - files are inherently stale
Graceful degradation pattern: io_utils fallbacks ensure robustness when engine is unavailable during startup
WebSocket background threads should poll at 2-second intervals to balance responsiveness vs CPU overhead
Test classes should be organized by cycle/feature to make regression isolation easier
Dashboard-dependent integration tests should use skipTest() guards not pytest.mark.skip to allow runtime detection of live services
Compile Python source to .pyc before archiving to prevent import failures when .py is removed
